question: How do people measure repetitive manual work and how draining it is, and decide when to automate it?
found: Site reliability engineering names it toil - manual, repetitive, automatable, without enduring value - and keeps it within a budget. Perceived exertion is rated on one 0-10 scale (Borg CR10); workload can be split into six parts (NASA-TLX), too heavy for every record. Whether automation pays is time per occurrence times frequency (xkcd 1205). Toyota's jidoka makes the machine judge and stop itself, so no person stands by to judge.
